limitations: Desktop native Mobile correctness is not Android/Web or full-map acceptance. Custom _custom_features=mobile exercises the actual platform gate on the desktop export; it does not simulate hardware, drivers, thermals, touch or Android lifecycle.

No CPU/GPU timing or FPS claim. Some correctness runs overlap unrelated Godot processes; their PIDs are recorded and they were not altered. The two initial baseline runs used an older detector that could miss resolved Godot binary names; their concurrency is not established.
Native Mobile uses existing shared opacity blending without the GLES colour-conversion helper. Per-frame opacity updates and shadow rendering still cost work; not asserted cheaper on device.

34/36 baseline lighting control images are exact; two vary by at most 2/255 with no pixel exceeding that bound. Fourteen fade-probe images match production exactly. Small cross-run numerical residuals are recorded, not explained as measured performance or total pixel identity.

The test report light_limit field is the OpenGL setting, not a native Mobile light cap. Mobile has its own eight-per-type receiver limit. The small-atlas boundary case uses 1024, but most fixtures explicitly use 2048; neither is physical-device validation.
Full-map/caster-aware acceptance, static/dynamic map caching, actual Android fade cost, P6 shimmer/redraw evidence and other handoff priorities remain open.
